body:
Adults who use nicotine products share spaces with people who do not, and with children, pets and neighbors. Good manners cost nothing, and they keep conflict, complaints and tighter rules away. This guide sets out practical etiquette and responsibility for adult vapers and pouch users aged 21 and over: knowing the rules, asking before you use a product indoors, handling vapor and clouds, being considerate about smell, keeping products away from children and pets, looking after batteries, disposing of devices properly, traveling considerately, being honest about nicotine and being a good example. It is written as a set of habits, not a lecture. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice. We make no health claims.

## Know the rules first
Rules on vaping differ widely. Many workplaces, transit systems, schools, restaurants, bars, parks and public buildings restrict or ban it. Some landlords ban it in rental homes. Airlines ban use on board. Rules also differ for pouches. Before you use a product somewhere new, check the posted signs and local rules. Where you are unsure, assume you may not, and ask. See [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Ask before you use around others
In someone's home, car or private space, ask permission, and accept a no without argument. Outdoors, move away from entrances, windows and groups, especially where children are present. At a shared table, ask whether it is all right before you take a puff. Asking takes a moment and makes you a welcome guest.

## Keep clouds to yourself
Large clouds can bother people nearby, irritate sensitive eyes and noses, and trigger alarms in some buildings. If you enjoy big vapor, save it for a place that suits it, and lower your power or choose a mouth-to-lung device in shared spaces. See [cloud chasing vs flavor chasing](/blog/cloud-chasing-vs-flavor-chasing/) and [sub-ohm vs mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/).

## Mind the smell
Sweet and dessert flavors can carry a strong smell that lingers on clothes, in cars and in rooms. If you share a car or a flat, think about how others will experience it. Pouches have little smell, but used pouches should not be left around. Wash your hands and refresh your clothes if you will be near others.

## Do not use where you should not
Do not use products on public transport, in cars with children, near hospitals and schools, or anywhere signs forbid it. Do not use them near someone who has asked you not to. Do not use them while driving, because it takes your hands and attention away. These are matters of courtesy and, in many places, of law.

## Keep products away from children and pets
Never give or sell a vape, liquid or pouch to anyone under 21. Store devices, liquids and pouches in a closed drawer or box, out of reach and sight, preferably locked. Nicotine liquid can be hazardous if swallowed or spilled on skin, and pouches can be dangerous to a child or a pet. Clean spills at once, and keep cleaning supplies away. If a child or pet has swallowed something, call poison control or emergency services at once. See [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/).

## Be careful with batteries
Lithium batteries can overheat if damaged or misused. Charge devices on a hard surface, while you are nearby, with a suitable cable and adapter, and unplug them when full. Do not carry loose batteries in a pocket with coins or keys. Do not leave devices in hot cars or in direct sun. Stop using any device that is hot, swollen or leaking. See [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Dispose of products responsibly
Do not litter used devices, pods, cartridges or pouches. Take disposables and batteries to a recycling site that accepts them, and put used pouches in a bin. Do not pour liquid down the drain. Leaving devices on the ground harms the environment, and it hands critics a reason to restrict products for everyone. See [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## Travel considerately
Follow airline, transit and local rules. Carry devices and spare batteries in hand baggage, switched off or locked, and do not use them on board. Check rules at your destination, because they differ. See [traveling with vapes](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/).

## Be honest about nicotine
Nicotine is addictive, and it is fair to say so. If someone asks about your habit, answer honestly. Do not encourage non-users, and especially young people, to start. If you want advice about nicotine use, a healthcare professional can help. We are a retailer, we make no health claims, and we do not suggest that any product treats or prevents any condition.

## Be a good customer and a good neighbor
Buy from sellers that verify age and follow the rules. Sign for deliveries yourself, and do not have parcels left where minors could take them. Do not resell to anyone under 21, and do not share your account or orders. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/) and [how to choose a reputable online vape store](/blog/how-to-choose-a-reputable-online-vape-store/).

## Be a good example
Younger relatives and neighbors notice what adults do. Keep products out of sight, do not use them around children and answer questions plainly. A calm, responsible approach does more to reduce underage use than any lecture. We have no interest in selling to minors, and we expect our customers to feel the same.

## Handling conflict
If someone objects to your use, listen, apologize if appropriate and move away. You do not have to agree, but you gain nothing by arguing. If a business or landlord sets a rule, follow it. If you think a rule is unfair, raise it politely through the proper channels.

## A short checklist
- Know the rules where you are.
- Ask first, and accept no.
- Keep clouds and smell in check.
- Store products away from children and pets.
- Charge batteries carefully.
- Dispose of devices responsibly.
- Follow travel rules.
- Be honest about nicotine.

## A worked example
A customer visits a friend's home, where the friend has a young child. They ask permission before taking a puff, and the friend suggests the porch. The customer steps outside, away from the door and the window, takes a few gentle puffs, puts the device away and washes their hands before going back in. No one was bothered, and the friend was happy to invite them again. A few small habits made the difference.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is it rude to vape outdoors near others?
It depends. Move away from groups, entrances and children, and ask if unsure.

### Can I use a device in my car?
It is your car, but passengers, especially children, should not be exposed, and some places have rules.

### What do I do with an old device?
Take it to a recycling site that accepts electronics and batteries.

### Should I tell my employer?
Follow workplace policy. Many workplaces restrict use.

### How do I keep products from children?
Lock them away, out of sight, and clean up spills.

## Shop
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Etiquette in specific places
### At work
Follow the workplace policy. Do not use devices at your desk unless it is explicitly allowed, and do not leave them in shared spaces. If breaks are permitted, step outside, away from doors, and keep it brief.

### At a friend's or family member's home
Ask permission. If told no, go outside or wait. Do not leave devices, liquids or pouches where children or pets can find them, and take your used pouches or empty devices with you.

### In a rental home or hotel
Check the lease or the hotel's rules. Many ban use indoors, and cleaning fees for violations can be high. Smoke alarms can trigger from large clouds.

### In a car with passengers
Ask before using, and do not use with children aboard. Do not use while driving.

### At events and in crowds
Crowded places are where clouds and smell bother people most. If use is allowed, keep it discreet, and move to the edge of the crowd.

## Etiquette in online and business dealings
Be honest in your dealings with sellers. Do not use someone else's identity or card details. Do not ask a seller to bypass age or signature rules. Do not resell products to people who cannot buy them legally. Follow the terms you agree to, and contact support politely if something is wrong, with your order ID. See [how to contact support](/blog/how-to-contact-support/).

## Why this matters for adult users
Rules for products like these are shaped partly by how visible and considerate users are. Courtesy reduces complaints and makes it easier for adults to keep access to products. It is also simply good manners, and it costs nothing.

## One more habit
Before you leave a place where you have been using a product, check that you have everything, including devices, spare pods, pouch cans and any packaging, and that you have left no mess. Pick up used pouches and empty packaging, and put them in a bin. Leaving a space as you found it is the simplest form of respect, and it keeps hosts, venues and neighbors willing to welcome adult users.
